newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel unchanged, buying interest thin.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel unchanged, buying interest thin.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was little changed on Thursday but buying interest was said to be thin.
One Scandinavian seller said he was not actively offering as there were no buyers seen on the market, but added he would do $100 a tonne.
"There's no one there at the other end. But if somebody comes along with three figures, say $100 or more, we'll have a deal," he said.
A second seller with July 0.5-0.7 percent material was also heard at $100 while a third seller that was more relaxed was a little higher. One buyer was heard sticking to his $97 a tonne.
Russian High sulphur straight-run was being offered at steady to higher prices.
Some traders said a seller was asking $84/$85 cif while others said two or three cargoes were being offered at two means plus $2/$3.
However, one of the cargoes, an M-100 already on the water, would be pressured if not sold soon, traders added.
